name: Pettenedda
body:
Pettenedda
CR 5

This fearsome hag garbed in rough woolens rakes awful foot-long clawed black fingernails through an immense mane of long, tangled black hair stretching down to her knees.

XP 1,600
NE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft; Perception +13

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 12, flat-footed 16 (+2 Dex, +6 natural)
hp 52 (7d10+14)
Fort +5, Ref +7, Will +8
Resist cold 5; SR 16; Weaknesses self-loathing

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 30 ft.
Melee 2 claws +11 (1d4+3 plus bleed)
Special Attacks captivating, bleed (1d6)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 7th, concentration +10)

At will—hidden presence (DC 15)
3/day—suggestion (DC 16)
1/day—bestow curse (DC 16)

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 12, Wis 16, Cha 17
Base Atk +7; CMB +10; CMD 22
Feats Combat Casting, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Bluff), Weapon Focus (claw)
Skills Bluff +16, Climb +11, Perception +13, Sense Motive +13, Stealth +12, Swim +20
Languages Common, Giant
SQ amphibious, hair effigy

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Captivating (Su)

By brushing one of her claws through her hair, a pettenedda can captivate listeners with the sound of running water. All listeners within a 60-foot spread must succeed on a DC 15 Will saving throw or become captivated. A creature that successfully saves is not subject to the same pettenedda’s ability for 24 hours. A victim who is captivated moves toward the petteneda using the most direct means available. If the path leads them into a dangerous area such as through fire or off a cliff, the creature receives a second saving throw to end the effect before moving into peril. Captivated creatures can take no actions other than to defend themselves. A victim within 5 feet of the pettenedda offers no resistance to her attacks. The pettenedda may maintain this effect with a move action. This is a sonic mind-affecting charm effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Hair Effigy (Su)

A pettenedda can cut some of her hair and spend 1 minute braiding and tying it into the form of a small doll, bracelet, or other decorative thing. A creature possessing a hair effigy adds a +1 luck bonus on all d20 rolls. Any creatures except a hag within 30 feet of the possessor take a -1 penalty on all d20 rolls.

In addition, she may scry (DC 17) on any creature possessing a hair effigy as a full-round action. She treats the target as familiar and as possessing their hair. A failure to scry will expend the hair effigy’s magic. A pettenedda can have three active hair effigies.

She always knows the approximate location of her active effigies and may turn them mundane as a free action.

Self-Loathing (Ex)

While a pettenedda is aware that her tangled hair always has another snarl, when confronted with her clear reflection (such as from a mirror), she begins to untangle her hair.

She must make a DC 16 Will save or become fascinated so long as she can see her reflection.

ECOLOGY

Environment any urban, ruin, or fresh water
Organization solitary or coven (3 hags of any kind)
Treasure standard

A pettenedda is an emaciated crone whose features are nearly obscured by a matted tangle of hair that cascades down to her knees. Pettenedda are set apart from their sister hags by this wild mess of hair, which may be longer than the pettenedda is tall, and for their wicked claws the size of daggers, which are forever running through their hair, attempting in vain to remove all the knots and snarls. Legend says that pettenedda were once human, cursed with their current state for the sin of vanity.

Pettenedda enjoy disrupting others’ routines and inconveniencing them and manipulate those around her to work against the self-interest of themselves and their communities. The sounds of people arguing and lamenting their problems is sweet music to the ears of a pettenedda.

Pettenedda prefer to lair in wells. A pettenedda will inflict all manner of misery on those that use her well. She will snatch an unsuspecting person attempting to draw water, sometimes enslaving them, but always eventually devouring them when she gets too hungry. A pettenedda might pretend to be some benevolent elemental spirit inhabiting the well, encouraging coins or other valuables to be dropped down the well in exchange for wisdom or prophecies, typically lies dreamed up by the pettenedda to cause further trouble. The only good thing to come from a pettenedda lairing in a well is that it will never be damaged or fouled. A pettenedda is very protective of her well and the water in it and murderously retaliates against anyone that attempts to harm it in any way.
